evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 茹古涵今
evidence.excerpt_zh: 坦坦蕩蕩之南為茹古涵今五楹南向其後方殿為韶景軒四面各五楹韶景軒前東為茂育齋西為竹香齋又北為靜通齋（圓圓明園册）臣等謹按茹古涵今四十景之一也額為皇上御書韶景軒額恭懸軒内其外南簷額曰喜接南薰東簷額曰景麗東皇西簷額曰翠生西嶺北簷額曰清風北户與竹香齋額皆御書茂育齋静通齋額皆世宗御書
evidence.summary: South of 坦坦蕩蕩: the five-bay 茹古涵今 facing south; behind it the square 韶景軒 of five bays per side, with a plaque on each of its four eaves; 茂育齋, 竹香齋 and 靜通齋 around it.

evidence.title: 静通斋: 乾隆四十年 poem of the Qianlong Emperor
evidence.date: 乾隆四十年 (1775), date from the compilation
evidence.excerpt_zh: 天地贞元运大公，澄观理亦易为穷。纷兹动植含春意，孰不权舆静以通。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Qianlong Emperor at 静通斋, 1775, on reading. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 静通斋
evidence.locator: v2 p.57, under 茹古涵今; source ref 12-958
evidence.excerpt_zh: 人情盖与止水同，澄之则清淆则浊。淆为动而澄为静，动斯扰矣静斯觉。楣端两字额静通，是义诚宜细研榷。苟非物来而顺应，未足言通劳把捉。
evidence.summary: Poem 静通斋 by the Qianlong Emperor, 1777, filed by the editors under 茹古涵今.

evidence.title: 静通斋: 乾隆五十四年 poem of the Qianlong Emperor
evidence.date: 乾隆五十四年 (1789), date from the compilation
evidence.excerpt_zh: 濓溪太极说，圣人常主静。通书更注之，明通理堪省。内外交相养，无欲挈要领。斋额仰奎文（斋额乃皇考所题也），不敏愿勉黾。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Qianlong Emperor at 静通斋, 1789, on reading. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 静通斋
evidence.locator: v2 p.58, under 茹古涵今; source ref 17-36
evidence.excerpt_zh: 濂溪太极说，圣人常主静。通书更注之，明通理堪省。内外交相养，无欲挈要领。
evidence.summary: Poem 静通斋 by the Qianlong Emperor, 1789, filed by the editors under 茹古涵今.

evidence.title: 静通斋: 乾隆五十九年 poem of the Qianlong Emperor
evidence.date: 乾隆五十九年 (1794), date from the compilation
evidence.excerpt_zh: 静通岂谓廊相接，理具濓溪太极图。中正及仁义以定，立人极合主斯夫。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Qianlong Emperor at 静通斋, 1794, on reading. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 圆明园百景史事分景汇编: 静通斋
evidence.locator: from p.130, under 茹古涵今
evidence.summary: 静通斋: 4 dated items, 1775-1794, of which 4 poems (Qianlong); recurring themes: reading. First dated 1775, last dated 1794.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
